notes: Polite form; to a friend: Jak se máš? Czechs answer it honestly, not just with 'fine'.

examples.tl: – Jak se máte? – Dobře, děkuju. A vy?
examples.en: – How are you? – Fine, thank you. And you?

notes: Literally 'I have myself well'. Short answers: Dobře = fine, Jde to = not bad.

examples.tl: Děkuju, mám se dobře. A vy?
examples.en: Thank you, I'm fine. And you?

notes: Polite form; to a friend: Jak se jmenuješ?

examples.tl: – Jak se jmenujete? – Jana. A vy?
examples.en: – What is your name? – Jana. And you?

notes: Jmenuju se + your own name. Simpler: Já jsem Tom. Formal spelling: jmenuji se.

examples.tl: Dobrý den, jmenuju se Tom a jsem z Ameriky.
examples.en: Hello, my name is Tom and I'm from America.

notes: Said with a handshake and eye contact when you are introduced.

examples.tl: – Já jsem Petr. – Těší mě, já jsem Tom.
examples.en: – I'm Petr. – Nice to meet you, I'm Tom.

notes: Polite form; to a friend: Odkud jsi?

examples.tl: – Odkud jste? – Z Ameriky, ale bydlím v Manile.
examples.en: – Where are you from? – From America, but I live in Manila.

notes: z + genitive: Amerika → z Ameriky. 'Z USA' is said 'z ú-es-á'.

examples.tl: Jsem z Ameriky, z Kalifornie.
examples.en: I'm from America, from California.

notes: Island groups take 'na', not 'v': na Filipínách, na Havaji. In Manila = v Manile.

examples.tl: Jsem Američan, ale bydlím na Filipínách.
examples.en: I'm American, but I live in the Philippines.

accept: I'm here for the first time.
This is my first time here.
notes: poprvé = for the first time; podruhé = for the second time.

examples.tl: V Česku jsem poprvé a moc se mi tu líbí.
examples.en: I'm in Czechia for the first time and I really like it here.

notes: Here for work = Jsem tady pracovně.

examples.tl: Jsem tady na dovolené, na deset dní.
examples.en: I'm here on vacation, for ten days.

notes: Líbí se mi + thing = I like how it looks or feels: Líbí se mi Praha. For food say: Chutná mi to.

examples.tl: Moc se mi tady líbí, Krumlov je nádherný.
examples.en: I really like it here, Krumlov is gorgeous.

notes: The all-purpose reaction to a view, a square or a church.

examples.tl: Ten výhled! To je krásné!
examples.en: That view! It's beautiful!

notes: Look each person in the eye as you clink glasses, and don't cross arms. Also said when someone sneezes.

examples.tl: Tak na zdraví!
examples.en: Well then, cheers!

notes: Mám rád + thing = I like it in general. A woman says: Mám ráda.

examples.tl: Mám rád české pivo a českou kuchyni.
examples.en: I like Czech beer and Czech food.

notes: Rád + verb = like doing something: rád cestuju (I like travelling). A woman says ráda.

examples.tl: Rád běhám a chodím po horách.
examples.en: I like running and hiking in the mountains.

notes: Liking food and drink only. The waiter or your host asks: Chutná vám?

examples.tl: – Chutná vám? – Ano, moc mi to chutná.
examples.en: – Do you like it? – Yes, I like it a lot.

notes: Even a few words win real goodwill: few visitors try.

examples.tl: Učím se česky, ale je to těžké.
examples.en: I'm learning Czech, but it's hard.

accept: What do you do for work?
notes: Can also mean 'what are you doing?'. Answer: Pracuju jako… (I work as…) or Pracuju v… (I work in…).

examples.tl: – Co děláte? – Pracuju v IT.
examples.en: – What do you do? – I work in IT.

notes: Literally 'how many years are to you?'. To a friend: Kolik ti je?

examples.tl: – Kolik vám je let? – Dvacet pět.
examples.en: – How old are you? – Twenty-five.

notes: Je mi + number (+ let). Swap in your own age: třicet = 30, dvacet osm = 28.

examples.tl: Je mi dvacet pět a bratrovi třicet.
examples.en: I'm twenty-five and my brother is thirty.

notes: Casual versions: Fakt? Vážně? (seriously?)

examples.tl: – Bydlím v Manile. – Opravdu? To je daleko!
examples.en: – I live in Manila. – Really? That's far!

en: Can we say 'ty' to each other?
notes: tykat = use familiar ty, vykat = use polite vy. The older person or the woman offers; don't switch on your own.

examples.tl: – Můžeme si tykat? Já jsem Petr. – Rád, já jsem Tom.
examples.en: – Can we say 'ty' to each other? I'm Petr. – Gladly, I'm Tom.

notes: Friendly goodbye in the polite form. To a friend: Měj se.

examples.tl: Děkuju za všechno, mějte se hezky.
examples.en: Thank you for everything, take care.

notes: Shop staff say it as you leave. Reply: Vám taky = you too. Hezký večer / víkend work the same way.

examples.tl: – Hezký den! – Děkuju, vám taky.
examples.en: – Have a nice day! – Thank you, you too.

notes: Literally 'happy journey'. You will hear it when you check out.

examples.tl: – Zítra letím domů. – Tak šťastnou cestu!
examples.en: – I fly home tomorrow. – Well, have a good trip!

notes: Casual hi and bye among friends, from Italian ciao. Not for staff or older strangers.

examples.tl: Tak čau, uvidíme se zítra.
examples.en: Bye then, see you tomorrow.

notes: A woman is an Američanka. The noun is capitalized; the adjective americký is not.

examples.tl: Jsem Američan, ale žiju v Asii.
examples.en: I'm American, but I live in Asia.

notes: A woman friend is a kamarádka. 'Přítel' and 'přítelkyně' usually mean boyfriend and girlfriend.

examples.tl: Jsem tady s kamarádem.
examples.en: I'm here with a friend.

notes: Declines like an adjective: na dovolenou = (going) on vacation, na dovolené = (being) on vacation.

examples.tl: Kam jedete na dovolenou?
examples.en: Where are you going on vacation?

notes: ve městě = in town. Staré Město = the Old Town of Prague.

examples.tl: Brno je druhé největší město v Česku.
examples.en: Brno is the second largest city in Czechia.

notes: The short everyday name. v Česku = in Czechia. Čechy = Bohemia (the west), Morava = Moravia (the east).

examples.tl: Jak se vám líbí v Česku?
examples.en: How do you like it in Czechia?

notes: The language as a noun. 'In Czech' is the adverb česky: mluvím česky. Angličtina / anglicky work the same way.

examples.tl: Čeština je těžký jazyk.
examples.en: Czech is a difficult language.

notes: krásný / krásná / krásné. Even stronger: nádherný.

examples.tl: Praha je krásné město.
examples.en: Prague is a beautiful city.

notes: Mild all-purpose praise for things, weather and people. Adverb: hezky.

examples.tl: Máte tady hezký výhled.
examples.en: You have a nice view here.

notes: Masculine although it ends in -a. Also means a hiker. A woman is a turistka.

examples.tl: V létě je v centru hodně turistů.
examples.en: In summer there are a lot of tourists in the center.
